SLIIT Research Project 2025-2026

ElderMeds

Intelligent medication support, designed around older adults.

A multimodal voice-vision assistant that brings medication adherence, safety reasoning, caregiver awareness, and supportive engagement into one connected research platform.

Explore the Research Read the Paper

The Challenge

Medication support needs more than reminders.

Medication non-adherence in older adults can be shaped by polypharmacy, memory limitations, changing daily routines, visual or motor limitations, adverse-drug concerns, medication-safety questions, and emotional or social factors.

Traditional reminder systems mainly answer "When should I take my medicine?" ElderMeds goes further by connecting reminders, verification evidence, safety reasoning, engagement, caregiver visibility, and conversational access through one shared longitudinal context.

Beyond Reminder Apps

  • What medicine should I take?
  • How many should I take?
  • Is this the expected medicine?
  • Was the intake workflow completed?
  • Is there a medication-safety concern?
  • Can my caregiver understand what happened?
  • Can I access records conversationally?

Research Gap

From Fragmented Tools to One Coordinated Elder-Care Platform

Many existing systems address medication reminders, recognition, safety, emotional support, disease-risk awareness, caregiver monitoring, or conversational health access separately. ElderMeds targets the fragmentation between these tools through shared patient and medication context.

Research Problem & Solution

Older adults need more than a medication alarm.

The central problem is not simply forgetting a reminder. Older adults may need support to identify the correct medicine, take the prescribed quantity, understand potential safety concerns, remain emotionally and cognitively engaged, and share meaningful information with caregivers.

01 / The Problem

Medication and wellbeing support remains fragmented.

Most existing applications solve only one part of the care journey. Reminder apps usually depend on the user pressing a "Taken" button, while medicine recognition, safety checking, emotional support, risk-awareness, and caregiver monitoring operate as separate tools with separate records.

  • The system cannot confirm that the correct medicine and quantity were presented.
  • Self-reported intake provides limited evidence and may not reveal missed, extra, or unexpected medicine.
  • Medication-safety advice may ignore allergies, interactions, chronic conditions, age, and polypharmacy.
  • Caregivers lack one understandable view of adherence, safety, engagement, and risk information.
  • Older adults must navigate several disconnected interfaces with little shared context.
02 / The Proposed Solution

One coordinated, multimodal elder-care platform.

ElderMeds connects four research components through shared, user-scoped longitudinal records. Voice, vision, deterministic rules, machine learning, and retrieval-grounded conversation work together while preserving clear decision-support boundaries.

  • Routine-aware reminders guide the elder at an appropriate daily moment.
  • Computer vision checks pill count and medicine-identity evidence before intake is recorded.
  • Hybrid safety assessment combines personal clinical context with pharmacovigilance evidence.
  • Emotional and cognitive activities provide bounded, non-diagnostic daily engagement.
  • A unified dashboard gives elders and caregivers grounded access to permitted records.
Central Research Question

How can a single multimodal and explainable platform improve medication-adherence support for older adults by combining verified intake, personalized safety screening, emotional and cognitive engagement, caregiver awareness, and grounded access to longitudinal health records?

Research Components

Four equally important parts of one care platform

Each component addresses a distinct challenge faced by older adults and caregivers. Together, they create a continuous loop from medication planning and verification to safety, daily engagement, and understandable health-record access.

Component 01

Intelligent Medication Reminder & Verified Intake

Moves beyond alarm-based reminders by checking what medicine is present, whether the dose is correct, and whether the intake workflow was completed.

Research focus
Medication adherence and objective intake verification
Core approach
Routine-aware scheduling and a five-gate Medication Intake Monitoring and Verification workflow
Intelligence
YOLO11n pill counting, visual medicine-identity retrieval, and MediaPipe hand-to-mouth analysis
Delivers
Correct, underdose, overdose, missing, or unexpected-medicine outcomes with adherence, stock, and caregiver updates

How it works

  1. Plan: Reminder times are calculated from the elder's breakfast, lunch, dinner, and sleep routines instead of using unrelated fixed alarms.
  2. Check: The user photographs the tablets. YOLO11n counts them while visual features and reference matching provide medicine-identity evidence.
  3. Verify: The detected medicines and quantities are compared with the active prescription, followed by hand-to-mouth motion analysis and manual swallowing confirmation.
  4. Record: The dose result is saved, tablet stock is updated, and important mismatches or low-stock conditions can be surfaced to the caregiver.

Practical value It provides stronger adherence evidence than a user simply tapping a "Taken" button, while still acknowledging that camera-observed motion does not prove swallowing.

Computer VisionVoiceYOLO11nMediaPipe
Component 02

Personalized Medication-Safety Assessment

Evaluates medication concerns using the individual patient's health context together with evidence learned from population-level adverse-event records.

Research focus
Explainable, patient-aware medication-safety decision support
Core approach
Hybrid scoring with 60% deterministic clinical rules and 40% calibrated pharmacovigilance ML evidence
Intelligence
Allergy, interaction, condition, age, polypharmacy, renal and hepatic checks combined with FAERS modelling
Delivers
Safe, Warning, or Dangerous screening with contributing factors and auditable explanations

How it works

  1. Normalize: Medicine names are standardized and matched with structured medication knowledge before the assessment begins.
  2. Personalize: Deterministic rules inspect allergies, drug interactions, previous reactions, chronic conditions, age, polypharmacy, and renal or hepatic considerations.
  3. Estimate: A calibrated model adds population-level evidence learned from 528,000 processed FAERS adverse-event records.
  4. Explain: Rule and model evidence are combined into a bounded safety category with the main contributing factors retained for review.

Practical value It makes the screening result traceable and patient-aware, but remains decision support rather than an individual causal prediction or prescribing decision.

Hybrid AIFAERSDDInterExplainability
Component 03

Emotional & Cognitive Engagement

Supports everyday wellbeing through brief, accessible interactions designed for companionship, cognitive stimulation, reflection, and continuity.

Research focus
Non-diagnostic emotional support and adaptive cognitive engagement
Core approach
TALK, PLAY, REMEMBER, and REVIEW experiences tailored by preferences, recent activity, and conversation context
Intelligence
Emotion classification, bounded five-turn conversations, activity recommendation, and consent-based remembered topics
Delivers
Supportive acknowledgements, varied cognitive activities, Life Book memories, and non-clinical wellness summaries

How it works

  1. Talk: A short five-turn conversation accepts voice, typed responses, or quick replies and uses emotion cues to select an appropriate supportive response.
  2. Play: Cognitive activities are adapted using the elder's preferences, recent choices, difficulty mode, and variety controls to avoid repetition.
  3. Remember: Life Book, Good Deeds or Pin Potha, and consent-based remembered topics support positive reminiscence while selected photos remain local.
  4. Review: Engagement history is summarized within non-clinical boundaries so the user and caregiver can observe patterns without diagnostic labels.

Practical value It encourages regular conversation, meaningful recall, and cognitive activity while treating emotion classification as a support signal, not a mental-health diagnosis.

Emotion AITALKPLAYREMEMBER
Component 04

Unified Conversational Dashboard

Turns records from every ElderMeds module into grounded answers, practical summaries, caregiver visibility, and carefully controlled actions.

Research focus
Secure conversational access to longitudinal elder-care information
Core approach
User-scoped retrieval, schema-restricted NL2SQL, trusted-source RAG, and confirmation-gated action execution
Intelligence
Local Llama 3 responses grounded only in validated records, with diabetes, stroke, and hypertension risk-awareness models
Delivers
Medication, adherence, safety, engagement, caregiver, and risk summaries with redaction and audit trails

How it works

  1. Understand: A natural-language question is interpreted against an allowlisted schema covering permitted ElderMeds record domains.
  2. Validate: Generated SQL is restricted to safe SELECT operations, parameterized by user identity, and checked before database execution.
  3. Ground: Retrieved rows are redacted where necessary and supplied to a local Llama 3 model that must answer from the available evidence.
  4. Act safely: Requested changes are converted into structured actions, shown in plain language, executed only after confirmation, and written to the audit trail.

Practical value It gives elders and caregivers one understandable access point for records and risk-awareness results without allowing unrestricted database queries or autonomous clinical actions.

NL2SQLRAGLlama 3Risk Awareness

Architecture

Layered System Architecture

Layer 1

Mobile / User Layer

React Native, Expo: scheduling, camera capture, voice interaction, safety results, emotional support, risk-awareness, caregiver interface.

Layer 2

Backend / Application

Node.js, Express: authentication, orchestration, access validation, deterministic safety logic, persistence, audit handling.

Layer 3

AI / ML Services

FastAPI: YOLO11n, NLP, safety ML, emotion classification, disease-risk models, local LLM, explainable AI.

Layer 4

Shared Data Layer

PostgreSQL, Supabase: profiles, routines, medications, adherence events, allergy histories, emotional sessions, alerts, predictions, audit records.

Methodology

Persist, Validate, Retrieve, Explain

Each module writes structured evidence to PostgreSQL tables. The dashboard retrieves records through deterministic summary queries or validated open-ended conversational paths, allowing cross-module context without direct in-memory coupling.

Agentic Action Layer

Conversational request -> structured action -> plain-language summary -> user confirmation -> execution -> audit log -> navigation to updated record.

Trusted Health-Advice Retrieval

Guideline-style questions use curated WHO, CDC, American Heart Association, and Sri Lanka NCD-related sources. The local LLM is constrained to retrieved evidence and recorded risk context.

Disease Risk-Awareness

Diabetes, stroke, and hypertension outputs are trained ML classification results used for non-diagnostic user awareness, not autonomous diagnosis.

Responsible use

Medication-safety outputs are decision-support signals. Disease-risk outputs are awareness aids. Emotion labels are non-diagnostic. ElderMeds is not intended for autonomous clinical diagnosis or prescribing.

Scientific Boundaries

Limitations & Future Work

Research Limitations

Pill counting used a held-out set from the same public manifest; independent external validation is still required. Emotion evaluation used a 140-response frozen domain set. Medication-safety controller labels are proxy labels, not clinician-adjudicated clinical ground truth. Stroke has low precision. Hypertension shows near-chance discrimination.

Future Work

Priorities include independently sourced pill-counting cohorts, varied devices and illumination, broader pill morphologies and occlusion tests, larger older-adult emotion datasets, blinded clinician/pharmacist medication-safety studies, stronger disease-risk datasets, usability evaluation, and real-world validation.
